question: Where do the MOST camels live?

post.premise: The land of the camel is not where most camels live
post.bait: Saudi Arabia, Australia or Somalia — which did you pick? 👇
keywords: which country has the most camels
post.sources_line: FAO; Worldmapper; Britannica; Australian Government DCCEEW

youtube.title: Which country has the most camels? It's not Arabia 🐪
youtube.description:
Saudi Arabia, Australia or the third one? The land everyone pictures with camels keeps under two million of them. One country has the biggest herd on Earth — millions more than Arabia — while the biggest WILD herd roams a continent where camels are not even native.
Guess before the map lights up, then see the table, the assumption wiped off the screen, and where camel milk is sold in every town.
Which did you pick?

threads.text: Which country has the most camels — Saudi Arabia, Australia or Somalia? The land everyone pictures keeps under two million of them; one country has the biggest herd on Earth, millions more, while the biggest wild herd roams a continent where camels are not even native.

intent: Wipe the assumption off the screen: the table that puts the Horn of Africa above Arabia, the word ARABIA erased, then the wild herd on the wrong continent and the milk in every Somali town.

v04.text: Somalia. More than 7 million camels, the most of any nation, in a country of 18 million people.

v05.text: Sudan follows with about 5 million, Kenya around 3. Saudi Arabia, the land of the camel, keeps under 2 million.

v06.text: And Australia? Camels are not native there, yet about 300,000 feral ones roam the outback, more than anywhere.

v07.text: In Somalia the camel is food, transport and wealth; its milk is sold in every town.

research.topic: Country with the most camels: Somalia (FAO live-animal stocks, 7 million+), then Sudan and Kenya; Saudi Arabia under 2 million; Australia holds the largest feral (wild-living) herd, estimated at roughly 300,000.

myths.myth: Saudi Arabia has the most camels because camels mean Arabia.
myths.reality: FAO stock data put Somalia first with more than 7 million camels; Saudi Arabia keeps under 2 million.

landscape.our_gap: Feed clips name Somalia as a one-liner; nobody builds the table against Arabia, wipes the assumption off the screen and then sets Australia's feral herd against it on a moving map.

worldmapper.notes: the world's largest camel population — more than 7 million — lives in Somalia, followed by Sudan and Kenya; first country outside Africa is Pakistan in 8th place

dcceew_camels.notes: camels introduced to Australia in the 19th century; feral population in the arid interior, estimated at about 300,000 after the 2009–13 control programme; the largest wild dromedary herd in the world
